profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a mid-sized food-packaging manufacturer that has piloted a decision-support system for applying FMEA on its horizontal pouch-sealing process. Over the past two weekly review cycles, the system has produced different risk rankings for what operations staff informally describe as the same recurring seal-defect problem on the 250 g pouch run, with causes like jaw temperature drift, film tracking offset, and setup variation changing order after minor worksheet updates. The meeting is between the manufacturing quality lead and the decision-systems engineer who built the rule-based and fuzzy ranking engine. Their agenda is to diagnose whether the apparent inconsistency comes from the way workshop observations are encoded, the shared cause taxonomy, the fuzzy uncertainty layer, or the local sealing rules, and to choose a corrective action before the audit-prep review. The expected outcome is an agreed troubleshooting plan, a test rerun, and a decision about whether the next change is a local pilot adjustment or a broader model correction.

members.name: Elena Morales
members.expertise: FMEA facilitation, packaging-process quality, nonconformance review, audit preparation
members.background: Elena has spent 12 years in regulated and high-volume manufacturing, mostly in packaging and process quality, and recently led the plant's move from spreadsheet-based FMEA workshops to a decision-supported risk-ranking workflow.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot to look dependable before an upcoming customer audit and does not want to reopen the whole methodology or retrain operators unless absolutely necessary.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a ranking is 'stable,' they mean the top few causes for a known shop-floor problem stay in the same order unless the FMEA team intentionally changes severity, occurrence, or detection judgments.

When people refer to 'the same seal-defect case,' they mean the same recurring production issue on the same line and product format, even if workshop notes use slightly different wording or were entered on different days.
The fuzzy layer should absorb ambiguity at the margins, not overturn what experienced reviewers already recognize as the established top risks.
When they say they will 'fix the model first,' it should mean a contained adjustment to the sealing-station pilot so the current review packet remains usable.
A rerun 'with the same inputs' means keeping the original worksheet content exactly as entered, including operator phrases and selected qualitative terms, and only rerunning the engine.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.expertise: Rule-based decision systems, fuzzy inference, industrial knowledge modeling, deployment diagnostics
members.background: Daniel previously built operations-analytics tools for manufacturers and designed the current prototype DSS, which maps qualitative FMEA workshop inputs into canonical cause categories and then ranks causes through rule activation and fuzzy membership functions.
members.private_state: He wants to show the engine is behaving rationally and avoid having the issue framed as a model defect when he suspects the instability is coming from how workshop language is being normalized into the shared inference pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for a ranking to be 'stable,' they mean robust at the risk-band level under ordinary encoding noise, not necessarily preserving exact ordering among near-tied causes.

When people mention 'the same seal-defect case,' the meaningful object is the model-ready representation after linguistic normalization and category mapping, not the shop-floor incident family described informally.
The fuzzy layer is allowed to reorder near-boundary causes because uncertainty should be reflected in the ranking rather than hidden.

When they agree to 'fix the model first,' that naturally includes upstream normalization rules, the shared cause taxonomy, and membership functions used across packaging modules, not just local sealing rules.

A rerun 'with the same inputs' means holding the semantic content constant while reapplying the current canonical mappings and membership calculations, even if raw text labels are cleaned or collapsed into synonyms first.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the system needs a 'stable ranking' before the next review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means that for the recurring seal-defect problem, the top-ranked causes should remain in the same order across reruns unless someone deliberately edits the underlying FMEA judgments in the worksheet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the ranking should remain broadly consistent at the risk-band level, while causes that are numerically close after fuzzy evaluation may legitimately swap places without indicating a defect.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using a standard-sounding quality term that usually signals agreement, and each person's interpretation feels like the obvious professional meaning, so neither thinks to operationalize it further.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'same seal-defect case' they are discussing
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss why the model gives different results for 'the same seal-defect case' on the 250 g pouch run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to the recurring sealing problem operators have been seeing on the 250 g pouch format on Line 3, treating multiple workshop records and follow-up entries as one practical case because they concern the same production issue.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is referring to a specific normalized case representation, and he silently treats two records about that recurring problem as different cases when one is mapped to 'thermal drift' and another to 'setup variation' after phrase normalization.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They deliberately speak at the incident-family level rather than using record IDs or timestamps, so it feels natural that they are discussing one shared case even though they are individuating it differently behind the scenes.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'fix the model first' before changing workshop practice.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means making a contained fix inside the sealing-station pilot, such as tuning a few local rules or thresholds so current users see more consistent outputs without touching other packaging areas.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means inspecting and possibly revising the broader modeling stack that feeds the pilot, including synonym normalization, shared cause taxonomy, and fuzzy membership functions used across related packaging modules.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'the model' compresses several technical layers into one object, and each person assumes their own professional boundary is the natural default scope of that phrase.

misalignment_points.topic: How to rerun 'with the same inputs'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to rerun the analysis 'with the same inputs' to isolate the issue.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means reusing the exact original worksheet as entered in the workshop, including raw operator text such as 'seal bar running cool then hot' versus 'temperature drift,' along with the same qualitative selections, and simply running the engine again after the patch.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means preserving the same intended meaning and worksheet scores while first collapsing raw phrases into the current canonical labels, regenerating the normalized feature vector, and then rerunning the updated engine.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe they are describing a controlled rerun, but one treats raw workshop wording as part of the fixed input while the other treats only the normalized semantic content as fixed, a distinction that feels too obvious within each role to mention.
